subject: Scoped hosting declaration, peering topology, and SOC-2/SIG deliverables
messages:
From: Emily Turner <emily.turner@medtech.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@medtech.com
Date: 2026-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial request — residency, privatelink, SOC 2 pack

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier. As part of our procurement/compliance review I need the following confirmed and packaged for our InfoSec team: 

1) A concise statement confirming that all customer production inference for our account can be scoped to EU-only regions (NO cross-border egress).
2) A network topology diagram showing your PrivateLink/peering architecture for Dedicated and Private deployments, including: Transit endpoints, peering circuits, and egress control points.
3) SOC 2 summary (controls mapped to hosting/residency), plus the latest CAIQ/SIG responses where you indicate anything relevant to KMS, HSM, and tenant segregation.

Can you send a single packet (PDF/CSV) we can upload to our vendor portal by EOD Wednesday? If there are any controls that require a configuration on our side (e.g., private peer, firewall ACLs, SAML config) call those out explicitly.

Appreciate it — Emily

--
Emily Turner
Senior Security Program Manager
MedTech Solutions

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@medtech.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial request — residency, privatelink, SOC 2 pack

Emily —

Thanks — we can absolutely package this. Summary / plan below, I copied our infra lead (Marcus) and solutions engineer (Priyom) to ensure we include operational steps.

Quick answers up front:
- Residency: we can pin inference serving to EU regions only (Frankfurt/Amsterdam). We do not route production inference traffic outside the selected region unless customer-configured replication or a failover policy triggers a cross-region fallback; that behavior is controlled by an explicit routing policy attached to the model endpoint.
- Private connectivity: we support both PrivateLink-style private endpoints for Hosted and VPC peering for Dedicated/Private deployments. Diagram and peering glossary will be attached.
- Cryptographic boundary: KMS-backed keying is customer-dedicated for Private deployments (BYOK); Hosted customers may use isolated tenant keys in our HSM-backed key store. We'll call out exact KMS key URIs in the packet.

Deliverables we will attach by EOD Wed: 
- redwood_privatelink_topology_v1.pdf (diagram + short ops notes)
- soc2-summary-2026.pdf (control mapping, attest date)
- sig-responses-compact.csv (SIG answers focusing on network/crypto/residency rows)

Operational notes for MedTech (brief):
- For Dedicated: request a private peering connection to the transit gateway (provide your ASN and prefix set). We will provide a peering playbook and an expected 2-week timeline for tunnel provisioning and validation.
- For Hosted + PrivateLink: configure an endpoint service consumer (VPC side) and accept our endpoint service. You will need to add a route for the endpoint prefix to your private subnet route table.
- Egress guardrails: we can enable a strict egress policy that drops any cross-region route advertisements; this is a switch on your account-level routing policy.

If acceptable I will attach the artifacts to this thread and Emily — please confirm any extra evidence you need (e.g., packet capture, traceroute proof) and we will include a one-time verification window.

Thanks,
Ava

--
Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@medtech.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-17T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial request — residency, privatelink, SOC 2 pack

Emily — following up with some engineering specifics you asked for during the call. Attaching the topology PDF and the compact SIG CSV. Highlights below.

Quoted for convenience:
- Private peering topology: we use an interconnect model where customer VPCs peer to a dedicated Redwood Transit Gateway in-region. The transit gateway enforces route tables scoped to the account and tenancy. We do not advertise customer prefixes outside the region.
- Cross-region failover: we consider a cross-region fallback a policy-level action — we will only enable it if explicitly requested in the endpoint's routing policy. By default failover is disabled.
- KMS and HSM: for Private installs (on-prem/VPC with private control plane) we support customer-controlled KMS keys (BYOK) and optional HSM tokenization for signing. For Hosted we provide tenant-isolated keys within our HSM cluster; HSM logs are available via the audit bundle.
- Tenant segregation: inference workloads run in isolated containers on dedicated GPU slices; metadata and artifacts are namespaced per account and stored in encrypted object storage with customer-specific prefixes.

Attachments in this message: redwood_privatelink_topology_v1.pdf; sig-responses-compact.csv; soc2-summary-2026.pdf.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with networking and security next week to go through the peering playbook and a checklist for your network ops team.

Regards,
Marcus
--
Marcus Lin
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
redwood.ai

From: Emily Turner <emily.turner@medtech.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial request — residency, privatelink, SOC 2 pack

Team — thanks for the packet and the quick turnaround. A few follow-ups before I upload to our vendor portal: 

1) Can you add a one-page statement (signed by Redwood Security) that explicitly says: 
   - "Inference traffic for MedTech Solutions under account MT-2048 will remain exclusively within EU regions unless MedTech requests cross-region failover in writing."
2) Under the KMS section please list the exact HSM provider and whether keys are multi-tenant or dedicated for Hosted customers (we need this for our crypto inventory).
3) On the peering playbook, include the RFC1918 prefix ranges you expect on the customer side in examples and a sample BGP config we can hand to our network team.

If you can attach those three small items (one-page legal-affirmation, HSM note, sample BGP snippet) I can finish the portal upload. Also please confirm the SOC 2 report date and auditor name on the summary page.

Once those are attached, we should be good. If it's easier to get the signed page first, send that and I'll start the portal flow — I can follow up with the other two items later this week.

Thanks — Emily

--
Emily Turner
Senior Security Program Manager
MedTech Solutions
